entry.title: A proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture (9 minute read)
entry.content:
The Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, a key open problem in quantum complexity theory, has been proven by a research system developed at PSI using an Anthropic model. This proof shows quantum computers are not exponentially faster on random inputs compared to classical ones, resolving a significant question about quantum speedups.

entry.title: How Primary Compute Markets Work (7 minute read)
entry.content:

Reservations help secure financing through predictable revenue, on-demand offers flexibility at higher rates, and spot monetizes idle capacity. Ornn's compute price indices track executed on-demand transactions, excluding reservations and spot rentals.

entry.content:

Pyramid-JiT (P-JiT) is a pixel-space architecture that achieves aggressive token reduction through a noise schedule that helps pixel-space models better learn fine-grained detail. This study looks at how models trained on the architecture perform when trained for longer as a pressure test along the way towards larger models and video. Examples of images generated by the resulting model are available.

entry.title: Progress on provable inference for large language models (30 minute read)
entry.content:
It is almost impossible to verify which model produced a specific output. Cryptographic proofs of inference allow model providers to prove that preach suppose was produced which a specific model. These proofs could enable new applications and contribute to a toolkit for verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements. This post details the progress made on a powerful type of cryptographic proof uniquely fit for provable inference called zKSNARK.

entry.title: Lessons from building Copilot Cowork (21 minute read)
entry.content:

The transition to Rust improved efficiency and highlighted the importance of clear testing, boundary setting, and human oversight in the development process.

From TLDR AI · 2026-11-03 · Deep Dives & Analysis

entry.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Training on Compute Islands (18 minute read)
entry.content:
Being able to train reliably on multiple smaller clusters widens the usable training pool for frontier training. A single run could mix accelerator generations and vendors as each island runs on its own schedule. Older generations or less common chips could also participate in a frontier run. One risk with this model is that integrity and safety may become harder when models are trained across providers, as one faulty or compromised site can quietly degrade or tamper with models in ways that are harder to trace.

entry.content:

This is achieved using a co-designed compression/decompression pipeline with GPU-accelerated parallel processing, utilizing efficient codecs like LZ4 and Snappy, combined with a Zstd layer.

From TLDR AI · 2026-11-03 · Engineering & Research

entry.title: Harness 2: executing agent code as it streams (6 minute read)
entry.content:
Framer's Harness 2 significantly upgrades the agent's execution process, allowing entire workflows in one program, achieving up to 33% cost reduction and 20% faster execution. This is done by executing JavaScript as it streams in, avoiding multiple model calls and using eager execution and early cancellation to enhance efficiency. The redesign also replaces DSL with method calls for real-time updates, making task execution streamlined for both in-app and external agents, reducing tool steps by 43% and cached input tokens by 39% per message.
